nodes.label: AI Layer Isolation
nodes.rationale: The ERP core is deterministic; addons/ai is read-only and advisory so AI output can never be the source of a ledger entry or stock movement. Made machine-checkable by having ai depend on base alone and reaching other addons via core contracts.

nodes.label: Money is Decimal Only
nodes.rationale: Never float. Ledger amounts NUMERIC(15,2), unit costs NUMERIC(12,4) to avoid float currency errors (NF14).

nodes.label: Multi-tenancy by organization_id
nodes.rationale: Every table carries organization_id and every query is scoped by it, no exceptions.

nodes.label: Server-side Totals
nodes.rationale: Client-supplied totals are never trusted or persisted.

nodes.label: Parameterized SQL Only
nodes.rationale: All DB access via SQLAlchemy ORM with bound parameters; never string interpolation (NF4).

nodes.label: Addon Layout
nodes.rationale: Business code lives in backend/app/addons/<name>/ with manifest, router, schemas, models, service, repository, permissions. Routers call services, services call repositories, repositories alone touch the DB. Adding an addon means adding a manifest, not editing main.py.

nodes.label: Addon Dependency Rule
nodes.rationale: An addon may import only from core and from addons in its manifest depends; enforced by test_addon_deps.py and addonDeps.test.ts so undeclared imports fail CI rather than review.

nodes.label: Frontend Layout Mirror
nodes.rationale: frontend/src/core for framework, frontend/src/addons/<name> per backend addon, with manifest.ts mirroring __manifest__.py. Cross-addon contributions go through core (overlays.ts) because the first S-05 overlay inverted the declared dependency direction.

nodes.label: Chart Boundary
nodes.rationale: No addon imports recharts; charts go through src/core/components/charts. ESLint blocks yAxisId and orientation=right because the design system forbids dual-axis charts.

nodes.label: Unwired Control Convention
nodes.rationale: Controls that would write data render visibly inert via the unwired prop; unwired.test.tsx checks every screen so wiring one up without removing the prop fails.

nodes.label: Eight Shared Addon Names
nodes.rationale: Frontend and backend share the same eight addon names (base, sales, inventory, procurement, accounting, ai, forecasting, home) so knowing the addon tells you where to look on both sides.

nodes.label: ADR 0001 Odoo-style Addon Layout
nodes.rationale: Eleven modules had no manifests, no loader, four owned no screen, and five parallel tracks would write into each other in Sprint 2. Adopted Odoo's structure (addon per domain, manifest depends, graph loader, registry) without Odoo's ORM, XML views or ir.* tables because building a framework does not fit 8.5 weeks. Rejected keeping eleven modules, full Odoo mimicry, Odoo short names, and unified res.partner.

nodes.label: Dependency Graph as Sprint Plan
nodes.rationale: Sprint 1 exercises no cross-addon edge; Sprint 2 lights up sales->accounting and procurement->accounting; Sprint 3 assembles home and ai from the registry.

nodes.label: core/registry.py
nodes.rationale: Addons contribute work queue rows, dashboard metrics, AI tools and rail entries to registry categories so home can render a queue fed by four addons while depending only on base.

nodes.label: AI Layer Isolation
nodes.rationale: ai declares only base so the dependency test makes the rule enforceable; the assistant sees operational data only via core/contracts/assistant.py with the organization taken from the session, never from the model; writes come back as drafts confirmed under normal role checks.

nodes.label: ForecastingWorker
nodes.rationale: Runs Holt-Winters in batch off the request path and returns INSUFFICIENT_DATA for products without enough history (R26, R28, R29; NF8, NF9, NF11).

nodes.label: Action-first Interface
nodes.rationale: The usual SaaS layout (sidebar, KPI cards, AI drawer) was dropped because it put reporting ahead of the work an ERP user has to do. Home is a work queue, every row carries its next action, record screens have one primary action in a bottom bar that previews side effects, and the AI has no tab.

nodes.label: ModuleRail
nodes.rationale: Navigation was settled twice: top tabs, then a 224px sidebar (2026-09-30), then a 72px rail plus breadcrumb module bar (2026-10-01). The rail keeps labels because an icon-only rail would leave six unlabelled glyphs; it leads with the organization, never a wordmark.

nodes.label: SectionNav
nodes.rationale: Sections are peers inside one module, deliberately not a fourth rail level; flattening would put eleven entries where there are five. Closed the hole where S-10 was reachable only by URL.

nodes.label: useRecordPager
nodes.rationale: Borrowed from Odoo; the cheapest thing that makes a back office feel quick, since moving between records otherwise means returning to the list.

nodes.label: Light-only Theme
nodes.rationale: Reversed the dark-first decision of 2026-10-01: small businesses doing their books use Odoo, Xero, QuickBooks, NetSuite, all light. Dropping the second theme removes a class of two-palette bugs and matches the light wireframes.

nodes.label: Color Tokens
nodes.rationale: One accent (blue) for primary actions; red and green only carry meaning. ink-faint raised to #747169 because #9E9B93 was 2.6:1 and failed AA. Tokens bound with @theme inline so var() resolves at the subtree.

nodes.label: Chart Color Ramp
nodes.rationale: Four-step ramp separate from the UI palette so a palette change cannot break chart readability. #8A8A8A chosen as the lightest gray clearing 3:1 with best colorblind separation, checked with WCAG luminance and CIEDE2000 under Machado 2009 dichromacy matrices. Wireframe #C8C6C1 rejected at 1.71:1.

nodes.label: Dual-axis Chart Ban
nodes.rationale: Two measures on two y-scales is the most common chart mistake. Enforced three ways: no wrapper exposes yAxisId, ESLint blocks recharts imports in addons, ESLint blocks yAxisId and orientation=right in the chart layer. S-10 resolved as two stacked charts sharing an x-axis and hover index; indexing to 100 rejected because an accountant wants the literal 15.1%.

nodes.label: ChartCard
nodes.rationale: Renders the same numbers as a visually hidden table for screen readers; tests assert on accessible names and table cells, not SVG nodes, because Recharts DOM is not a stable contract.

nodes.label: Typography (Inter + JetBrains Mono)
nodes.rationale: Replaced IBM Plex Sans/Serif/Mono on 2026-10-01; the serif's loss of distinctiveness was accepted knowingly. Mono is load-bearing for aligned digits in S-03, S-05, S-07, S-10. Self-hosted via @fontsource-variable to avoid a render-blocking round trip.

nodes.label: Motion Rules
nodes.rationale: Only transform and opacity animate; exits shorter than entrances. The documented stagger never shipped because Tailwind only emits literal class names; now a --rise-index property read by one rise utility. Reduced motion wraps the animation in no-preference rather than zeroing duration, which had pinned content at opacity 0.

nodes.label: Icon.tsx Path Registry
nodes.rationale: Hand-drawn 16px stroke 1.3 icons because no published set matches the house style; switch to lucide-react past about 35 icons so the decision has a trigger. Set stands at 28.

nodes.label: Button Variants
nodes.rationale: Blue is reserved; a screen has at most one blue button. Lists put the primary top right, records pin it to the ActionBar; S-05 was moved to the bar so the rule holds in one line.

nodes.label: The Unwired Convention
nodes.rationale: Rather than shipping buttons that look live and silently do nothing, writes render inert but focusable with aria-disabled and a tooltip. View state and navigation are live; writes and unbuilt screens are unwired. Button.test.tsx and screen tests assert it.

nodes.label: useAccess
nodes.rationale: Reads the role-by-area matrix from base/fixtures/people.ts to hide rail entries and queue groups. The interface only hides, never decides; RBACGuard enforces on the server. Fifth and last core file allowed to reach into an addon.

nodes.label: AnswerPanel
nodes.rationale: Every AI answer shows tool calls made, a summary with source chips per figure, and a draft marked not saved. Shared by Ask and Cmd-K so the two never drift.

nodes.label: screenshots.mjs Visual Pass
nodes.rationale: Captures all fourteen routes at 1280x800 and fails on console errors; Playwright deliberately not a dependency. Keeps finding things a green suite ships since tests check structure, not the page.

nodes.label: Feature List F1-F20
nodes.rationale: Original docstrings used F1-F14 with AI as F12/F14 and forecasting F13, written before the requirements doc existed; all re-tagged against F1-F20 during ADR 0001.

nodes.label: Six Roles (F2)
nodes.rationale: Owner, Admin, Sales, Inventory, Purchasing, Accounting. The S-09 wireframe shows only four roles and is wrong.

nodes.label: Requirements Traceability Matrix
nodes.rationale: Previous matrix was generated before the requirements doc existed; ten rows pointed at the wrong module and NF18-NF22 were missing. Authoritative mapping is the requirements key in each manifest, asserted by test_manifests.py.

nodes.label: Open Question: Order State Machines
nodes.rationale: F7 specifies a Closed state and F8 a Paid state; wireframes, fixtures and StatusPill have neither. Must be settled before sales and procurement are built.

nodes.label: Customer Portal Out of Scope
nodes.rationale: All six F2 roles are internal staff, no R-number asks for a portal, and it would need row scoping below organization_id. Customers are records, not users.

nodes.label: Screens S-11 to S-13
nodes.rationale: Added because the design doc named requirements (R5 Customer management, R18 Chart of accounts) it never drew; S-11 follows the S-03 list pattern and S-12 the S-05 record pattern.

nodes.label: Accounting Access Matrix
nodes.rationale: Role-by-action matrix RBACGuard enforces for the accounting addon; rows are still TODO (one per endpoint). Covers requirements R18-R23 and R31.

nodes.label: AI Access Matrix
nodes.rationale: Role-by-action matrix for the ai addon; rows TODO. Covers R25, R26, R27, R30.

nodes.label: Base Access Matrix
nodes.rationale: Role-by-action matrix for the base addon; rows TODO. Covers R1-R4.

nodes.label: Forecasting Access Matrix
nodes.rationale: Role-by-action matrix for the forecasting addon; rows TODO. Covers R28, R29.

nodes.label: Home Access Matrix
nodes.rationale: Role-by-action matrix for the home addon; rows TODO. Covers R24.

nodes.label: Inventory Access Matrix
nodes.rationale: Role-by-action matrix for the inventory addon; rows TODO. Covers R7-R12 and R31.

nodes.label: Procurement Access Matrix
nodes.rationale: Role-by-action matrix for the procurement addon; rows TODO. Covers R16, R17.

nodes.label: Sales Access Matrix
nodes.rationale: Role-by-action matrix for the sales addon; rows TODO. Covers R5, R6, R13, R14, R15.

nodes.label: Server-side RBAC enforcement, UI only hides
nodes.rationale: Every access.md states that RBACGuard reads the matrix and the UI only hides what a role cannot use. Authorization is enforced on the backend; hiding controls in the frontend is a convenience, not a security boundary.

nodes.label: Requirement R31 (shared by accounting and inventory)
nodes.rationale: R31 is the only requirement listed in two addon matrices (accounting and inventory), implying a cross-addon concern such as inventory valuation flowing into the ledger.

nodes.label: Sector 7 HTML App Shell
nodes.rationale: Single-page Vite entry document. Declares light-only color-scheme, an SVG favicon, and a meta description positioning Sector 7 as a small-business ERP that keeps sales orders, stock, purchase orders and the books in step.

nodes.label: Light-only color scheme
nodes.rationale: index.html sets meta color-scheme=light, so the browser never applies dark-mode form control defaults; the UI is designed as a single light theme.
